subject: Urban Planning
title: Land Readjustment: The Japanese Method
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Land Readjustment: The Japanese Method.

hook.text: In Japan, landowners pool their parcels, a government agency redesigns the area, and everyone gets a smaller but improved lot.

buildup.text: Land readjustment was used to rebuild Tokyo after the 1923 earthquake and again after World War II bombings.

discovery.text: Owners give up 30-40% of their land for roads, parks, and utilities. Their remaining lot is worth more because of the upgrades.

twist.text: No government money is needed. The increased land value funds the infrastructure. It's self-financing urban planning.

climax.text: Over 30% of all urban land in Japan has been shaped by land readjustment. It's the primary city-building tool.

punchline.text: Give up some land. Get better land back. The city funds itself.

quiz.question: How does land readjustment fund urban infrastructure?
options: Government bonds pay for all construction and are repaid through taxes
Increased land values from improvements fund the project without government money
Landowners pay a special assessment fee based on frontage
